transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because of my husband's sister. She’s been working this family business of ours, and... well, it's so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. 

My husband and other folks keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now, clear as day, and I'm just tired of being pushed aside.

When your husband or other family members tell you that the sister-in-law isn't trying to push you out, what do you think about what they're saying? Does any part of you consider that they might be right, or are you completely certain that your sister-in-law is doing this no matter what anyone tells you?

Well, like I was saying... no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I've been seeing. I'm absolutely certain of it. 

They can tell me I'm wrong all day long, but it's been going on for more than a year now. I see her working the family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. I'm not blind to it, even if my husband wants to pretend it's not happening. So no, I don't think they're right at all. I know exactly what she's doing.

Besides seeing your sister-in-law's actions at the business, have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had any other unusual perceptions that others around you couldn't explain or didn't experience?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's just... I just see what she's doing at the business. That's all. There's nothing unusual going on with my hearing or my eyesight, I just pay attention to how she acts.

When you think about your sister-in-law wanting to control the money and push you out of decisions, is this something that could realistically happen in a family business, or does it seem like something that goes against all normal logic and couldn't possibly be true in any way?

Well, yeah, it's something that could realistically happen. I mean, it happens in family businesses all the time, right? People get greedy. It's not like she's using magic or something crazy to do it. She's just... she's just maneuvering things, getting her hands on the accounts, talking to the right people to make sure I'm left out. It's completely possible, and that's exactly what she's doing.
Beyond your sister-in-law and the family business situation, do you find yourself being suspicious or distrustful of other people in your life — like friends, coworkers, or neighbors — in general?

No, not really. It's just her. I don't have any problems with my friends or neighbors or anyone else. I trust the people I've always trusted. It's just this specific situation with my sister-in-law and the business. I don't go around suspecting everyone of trying to do me wrong. It's just her.

When you think about why your sister-in-law is doing this — trying to control the money and push you out — do you have a clear understanding of her overall plan or goal, or is it more that you just notice her individual actions without seeing how they all fit together?

I'm not really sure if she has some big master plan, to be honest. I mean... I know she wants the money and wants me out, but I don't know exactly how she's putting it all together in her head. I just see what she's doing right in front of me. I notice the little things she does, like talking to the right people or messing with the accounts, but... I don't have all the pieces to her puzzle, I guess. I just know what I see her doing day to day.

If you saw clear evidence — like a video recording or a written document — that showed your sister-in-law wasn't actually trying to control the money or push you out, would that change your mind about what's happening, or would you still believe she's doing it anyway?

Honestly, no, it wouldn't change my mind. I mean... folks try to smooth it over all the time, saying I'm just misunderstanding things. But I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. My husband's sister has been working this family business specifically so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. A piece of paper or a video isn't going to change that, because I already know exactly what she's doing.

latest_inference.note: F22.9 ruled out. The patient's absolute conviction despite contrary evidence, refusal to consider alternative explanations, and circumscribed nature of the delusion (isolated to sister-in-law, not generalized suspiciousness) strongly support F22.0 over other psychotic or personality disorders.
